transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I’ve been feeling wound up and on edge for months, like my mood is stuck on high and I’m snapping at everyone, even my own family. It's gotten so bad that they finally brought me here because I just can't seem to calm down.
Have there been periods where you felt unusually energetic, slept very little, or felt like your thoughts were racing, even if you felt good during those times?

Yes, it feels like I have a motor inside me that won't shut off, and my mind is constantly racing with ideas. Most nights I only sleep two or three hours but I don't even feel tired, and this has been going on for about half a year now.

Have you experienced any distinct periods in your life, lasting at least a week, where you felt completely back to your normal self and mood, or has this high-energy, racing-thought state been your constant baseline for the last six months?

No, I haven't felt back to my normal self at all. For the last six months, I've mostly been in that wired, high-energy state, and even when I crash and feel totally flat and shut down, I still don't feel normal because the voices and the feeling of being watched never stop.
Do these voices and the feeling of being watched persist even when your mood is stable and you aren't feeling unusually energetic or depressed?

Yes, they definitely do. A couple of months ago, my mood felt pretty flat and drained instead of amped up, but those voices and the feeling that everyone was watching and testing me never let up during those weeks.

When you were feeling flat and drained, were the voices and the feeling of being watched directly related to your low mood, such as telling you that you were worthless or being punished, or did they persist independently of how you felt?

They definitely persisted on their own, independent of how I felt. Even though my mood was flat and drained, the voices didn't change and I still felt like people were watching and testing me. It was like those things were running on a completely separate track from my mood.

Have there been any periods of at least two weeks where you experienced these voices and feelings of being watched when you were NOT experiencing significant mood symptoms like being 'wired' or 'flat'?

Yes, a couple of months ago there was a period of a few weeks where my mood wasn't feeling super amped up or wired. Even during those weeks, the voices and the feeling of being watched and tested never let up.

During those weeks when your mood was stable, were the voices and the feeling of being watched your only major symptoms, or did you also experience other changes in your thinking, such as disorganized speech or a significant lack of motivation and social withdrawal?

During those weeks, it was pretty much just the voices and the feeling of being watched that stayed constant. I don't really recall having those other issues, like my speech being jumbled or that severe lack of motivation, during that specific time. It was mainly just the paranoia and hearing things that wouldn't let up.

During those weeks when your mood was stable, did you experience any other symptoms like a persistent belief that people were plotting against you or that your thoughts were being broadcast to others?

Yes, back then when my mood was more flat, the voices and that strong feeling that people at work and church were watching and testing me never stopped. I didn't feel like my thoughts were being broadcast, but I was absolutely sure they were plotting to get me fired.
Looking back over the last six months, have you spent more of that time experiencing the high-energy, 'wired' symptoms, or have you spent more time feeling the flat, drained, and depressed symptoms?

For most of this whole stretch, I've spent the vast majority of my time feeling revved up, wired, and overactive. I only have short spells where I crash and go quiet, but I quickly ramp right back up into that high-energy state.
During the times you were feeling revved up and wired, did you experience symptoms like hearing voices or feeling watched, or were those experiences only present when your mood was flat?

When I first started feeling super amped up and barely sleeping, that was actually when the voices really kicked in and I became convinced people were plotting against me. They both happened at the exact same time for months while I was wired. But like I mentioned, even when my mood crashed and felt flat later on, those voices and the feeling of being watched still didn't go away.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits prominent manic symptoms (elevated energy, racing thoughts, decreased need for sleep) alongside psychotic symptoms (auditory hallucinations, paranoid delusions). Crucially, the psychotic symptoms persisted for at least two weeks in the absence of prominent mood symptoms, confirming a schizoaffective presentation. Since the manic symptoms are predominant over the depressive symptoms, F25.0 is the most accurate classification.
